causal:influence:abat_activity:negative:.evidence: GABA-transaminase deficiency (ABAT, OMIM 613163) — elevated CSF GABA, beta-alanine, and taurine; Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (ABAT deficiency: elevated CSF taurine documented alongside GABA and beta-alanine); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (GABA-T/ABAT catabolizes gamma- and beta-amino acids). | intervention: do(ABAT LoF) — GABA-transaminase deficiency
causal:influence:abat_activity:negative:.mechanism: 4-aminobutyrate aminotransferase (ABAT) has substrate activity toward taurine (a beta-sulfinyl amino acid structurally analogous to beta-alanine); ABAT deficiency impairs taurine catabolism in addition to GABA and beta-alanine, causing taurine to accumulate in CSF alongside GABA and beta-alanine.

causal:influence:abcd1_activity:negative.evidence: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD, OMIM 300100): Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 'Disorders of peroxisome biogenesis and metabolism'; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, peroxisomal beta-oxidation; plasma C26:0 is the cardinal biomarker for X-ALD diagnosis | intervention: loss-of-function of ABCD1 gene (X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy, OMIM 300100)

causal:influence:acid_sphingomyelinase_a.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Lysosomal Storage Diseases' (Niemann-Pick disease type A/B: SMPD1 deficiency, sphingomyelin accumulation in tissues). causal:influence:acid_sphingomyelinase_a.mechanism: Acid sphingomyelinase (SMPD1) hydrolyzes sphingomyelin to ceramide and phosphocholine in lysosomes; loss-of-function (Niemann-Pick disease types A/B, OMIM 257200/607616) causes sphingomyelin to accumulate in lysosomes of macrophages, liver, spleen, lung, and brain.

causal:influence:aicar_transformylase_ac.evidence: ATIC/AICA-ribosiduria OMIM 608688; Casula et al., Am J Hum Genet 2009 (ATIC LoF: massive urinary AICA-riboside excretion); Ramond et al., JIMD 2020 (three additional ATIC deficiency cases). | intervention: do(ATIC LoF, OMIM 608688) — AICA-riboside accumulates and is excreted in urine

causal:influence:aicda_deaminase_activit.evidence: HIGM2 (OMIM 605258): absent IgG including IgG3; Muramatsu et al. Cell 2000. | intervention: do(AICDA LoF) — no class-switch to IgG3 [citations PubMed-verified]

causal:influence:aldolase_b_activity:pos.evidence: Hereditary fructose intolerance OMIM 229600 (ALDOB deficiency; hypoglycemia after fructose/sucrose ingestion is the cardinal acute manifestation). Steinmann et al. in Scriver's OMMBID 'Disorders of Fructose Metabolism' (fructose-1-phosphate accumulation inhibits glycogen phosphorylase and FBPase -> combined glycogenolysis + gluconeogenesis failure -> hypoglycemia). PMC11105038 (Bouteldja & Timson 2024 'Recent advances in the pathogenesis of HFI': F1P inhibits hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 15 (fructose catabolism: ALDOB in hepatocytes; F1P accumulation mechanism). OMIM 612724 (ALDOB gene entry). Intervention: do(ALDOB LoF, HFI, OMIM 229600) -> F1P accumulates -> inhibits glycogenolysis + gluconeogenesis -> plasma_glucose DOWN (hypoglycemia after fructose exposure). | intervention: do(ALDOB LoF, hereditary fructose intolerance, OMIM 229600) -> fructose-1-phosphate accumulation -> inhibition of glycogenolysis (glycogen phosphorylase) and gluconeogenesis (FBPase) -> plasma_glucose DOWN (acute hypoglycemia)
causal:influence:aldolase_b_activity:pos.mechanism: Hepatic aldolase B (ALDOB) cleaves fructose-1-phosphate (the KHK product) into dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde. ALDOB LoF (hereditary fructose intolerance, HFI, OMIM 229600) causes fructose-1-phosphate accumulation in hepatocytes: F1P competitively inhibits both glycogen phosphorylase (blocking glycogenolysis) and fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (blocking gluconeogenesis), while also depleting inorganic phosphate and ATP. The combined effect is severe fasting hypoglycemia after fructose ingestion. ALDOB activity -> F1P clearance -> restored glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis -> plasma glucose maintained.

causal:influence:aromatase_activity:posi.evidence: "a mean of 7 months of treatment with anastrozole demonstrated a substantial decrease in breast area (63%) and volume (53%), as measured manually and by ultrasonography" Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 26, p 1163–1164

causal:influence:aspartylglucosaminidase.mechanism: RHEA:11544 (EC 3.5.1.26): N(4)-(beta-N-acetyl-D-glucosaminyl)-L-asparagine (CHEBI:17261) + H2O = N-acetyl-beta-D-glucosaminylamine + L-aspartate + H(+); aspartylglucosamine (the N-glycan core aspartamide) is the substrate; AGA LoF causes lysosomal accumulation and urinary/plasma overflow

causal:influence:atp7b_activity:positive.evidence: OMIM #277900 Wilson disease (low serum ceruloplasmin); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (ceruloplasmin copper loading); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine
causal:influence:atp7b_activity:positive.mechanism: ATP7B in the hepatocyte trans-Golgi network loads copper onto apoceruloplasmin to form secreted holo-ceruloplasmin; without copper loading, apoceruloplasmin is rapidly degraded, so ATP7B loss lowers circulating (holo-)ceruloplasmin

causal:influence:bckdh_activity:negative.evidence: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD; BCKDHA/BCKDHB/DBT, OMIM 248600); Scriver's OMMBID: urine organic acid analysis in MSUD reveals elevated 2-oxoisocaproate (leucine keto acid) | intervention: genetic LoF of BCKDHA, BCKDHB, or DBT gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive MSUD)
causal:influence:bckdh_activity:negative.mechanism: BCKDH deficiency causes 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoate (2-oxoisocaproate) to overflow into urine — reduced BCKDH activity raises urinary 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoic acid

causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.evidence: Maple syrup urine disease / MSUD (OMIM 248600); NBK557773 — 'BCKD enzyme complex catalyzes the decarboxylation of the alpha-keto acids of leucine, isoleucine, and valine'; Wikipedia MSUD — 'large accumulation of the branched-chain amino acids leucine, isoleucine, and valine'; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18 (BCAA catabolism, BCKDH complex). | intervention: do(BCKDH complex activity ↓) = maple syrup urine disease (OMIM 248600)
causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.mechanism: The BCKDH complex (subunits BCKDHA/B) oxidatively decarboxylates the branched-chain alpha-keto acids derived from leucine, isoleucine, and valine; leucine is the most neurotoxic substrate. Reduced BCKDH activity → alpha-ketoisocaproate and leucine accumulate (∂[Leu]/∂(BCKDH activity) < 0). Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) is the canonical LoF.

causal:influence:bco1_activity:negative:.evidence: Hypercarotenemia and vitamin A deficiency (HCVAD) OMIM 115300, caused by heterozygous BCO1 (BCMO1) mutation T170M with ~90% reduced enzymatic activity leading to elevated serum beta-carotene; Molecular and dietary regulation of BCMO1 (von Lintig, Arch Biochem Biophys 2010); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (carotenoid metabolism, beta-carotene as provitamin A). | intervention: BCO1/BCMO1 loss-of-function (OMIM 115300, hypercarotenemia): plasma beta-carotene rises markedly
causal:influence:bco1_activity:negative:.mechanism: BCO1 (beta,beta-carotene 15,15'-dioxygenase) catalyzes the oxidative cleavage of beta-carotene to two molecules of retinal, which is the major catabolic route for circulating beta-carotene. Reduced BCO1 activity impairs this cleavage, causing beta-carotene to accumulate in plasma (hypercarotenemia). Edge sign is negative: more enzyme activity lowers plasma beta-carotene.

causal:influence:beta_hexosaminidase_b_a.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Sandhoff disease (HEXB deficiency, OMIM 268800) — urinary GlcNAc-rich oligosaccharides are a diagnostic feature; Williams Hematology / lysosomal storage disease references confirm oligosacchariduria. | intervention: HEXB loss-of-function (Sandhoff disease): do(beta_hexosaminidase_b_activity↓) → urinary GlcNAc-oligosaccharide excretion↑
causal:influence:beta_hexosaminidase_b_a.mechanism: Beta-hexosaminidase B (HEXB) cleaves N-acetylglucosamine residues from gangliosides, glycoproteins, and keratan sulfate in lysosomes. HEXB LoF (Sandhoff disease, OMIM 268800) causes both Hex A and Hex B enzymes to be deficient, leading to accumulation and urinary excretion of GlcNAc-rich GM2 ganglioside-derived oligosaccharides and glycoprotein fragments.

causal:influence:blood_gas_barrier_thick.evidence: "the measured diffusing capacity of the lung for CO depends not only on the area and thickness of the blood-gas barrier" and "inversely proportional to the thickness (T)" (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 3)
causal:influence:blood_gas_barrier_thick.mechanism: DL includes thickness in the denominator (Fick's law); thicker barrier lowers measured diffusing capacity

causal:influence:carboxylesterase_1_acti.evidence: PMID 24038130; (Abstract/Results (Hepatic carboxylesterase 1 is essential for both normal and farnesoid X receptor-controlled lipid homeostasis)); “knockdown of hepatic CES1 increased hepatic TG and plasma cholesterol levels” | do(reduce CES1) raises hepatic/plasma lipids (TG), so CES1 activity negatively affects plasma triglycerides. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:carboxylesterase_1_acti.mechanism: hepatic CES1 hydrolyzes intracellular triglycerides; hepatic CES1 knockdown causes hepatic TG accumulation with increased VLDL secretion and plasma lipids -> CES1 activity lowers circulating triglycerides

causal:influence:cardiomyocyte_intracell.evidence: Bers DM 2002 Nature 415:198-205 — quantitative analysis of NCX-mediated Ca2+ extrusion: rising [Na+]i slows NCX forward mode, increasing SR Ca2+ load and systolic Ca2+ transient; Bhatt DL et al and Digitalis Investigation Group 1997 NEJM 336:525 — digoxin (Na/K-ATPase inhibitor) raises [Na+]i, increases Ca2+ transient, positive inotropy; Sipido KR et al 1997 Circ Res 81:1174 — elevated [Na+]i in heart failure directly linked to reduced NCX efflux and elevated systolic Ca2+ transient amplitude. | intervention: do(cardiomyocyte_intracellular_sodium +) — digoxin (Na+/K+-ATPase inhibitor) raises [Na+]i, reducing NCX Ca2+ efflux, increasing cytosolic Ca2+ transient and contractility; do(cardiomyocyte_intracellular_sodium -) — ranolazine (late Na+ current inhibitor) lowers [Na+]i, reducing Ca2+ overload and Ca2+ transient amplitude. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cardiomyocyte_intracell.mechanism: The sarcolemmal Na+/Ca2+ exchanger (NCX1) operates electrogenically: in forward mode it extrudes 1 Ca2+ per cycle by importing 3 Na+. When cardiomyocyte intracellular [Na+] rises, the inward Na+ driving force for NCX is reduced, impairing Ca2+ efflux; this raises SR Ca2+ load and increases the amplitude of the cytosolic Ca2+ transient during systole (positive inotropy). This is the molecular mechanism of cardiac glycosides (digoxin): inhibiting Na+/K+-ATPase → [Na+]i rises → NCX Ca2+ efflux decreases → Ca2+ transient increases → stronger contraction.

causal:influence:cellular_cobalamin_upta.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (cobalamin coenzymes: methylcobalamin for methionine synthase); cblC/cblF/cblJ intracellular-cobalamin disorders reduce both coenzyme forms
causal:influence:cellular_cobalamin_upta.mechanism: intracellular cobalamin (from cellular uptake) is processed to methylcobalamin (the MTR / methionine-synthase coenzyme); reduced cobalamin uptake lowers methylcobalamin

causal:influence:cerebral_blood_flow:neg.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. causal:influence:cerebral_blood_flow:neg.mechanism: reduced flow to the medullary vasomotor center lets CO2 accumulate locally, directly exciting the sympathetic vasoconstrictor/cardioaccelerator neurons

causal:influence:coq2_activity:positive:.evidence: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency type 1 OMIM 607426 (COQ2 mutation as founding cause); Quinzii et al. AJHG 2006 PMID 16400613 (COQ2 Y297C mutation causes primary CoQ10 deficiency); GeneReviews NBK410087 (primary CoQ10 deficiency overview); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (ubiquinone biosynthesis in mitochondria). | intervention: COQ2 loss-of-function (primary CoQ10 deficiency, OMIM 607426): skeletal-muscle CoQ10 concentration falls [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:coq2_activity:positive:.mechanism: COQ2 (4-hydroxybenzoate polyprenyltransferase) catalyzes an early committed step in the mitochondrial coenzyme Q10 (ubiquinone) biosynthetic pathway, transferring the polyprenyl tail onto 4-hydroxybenzoate. COQ2 loss-of-function causes primary CoQ10 deficiency, with reduced ubiquinone levels in skeletal muscle and other tissues. More COQ2 activity supports higher tissue CoQ10 content.

causal:influence:csf_l_2_hydroxyglutarat.evidence: L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria (OMIM 236792, L2HGDH gene); Achouri et al. (2004) Biochem J — L-2-HG is a competitive inhibitor of alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase; L2hgdh Deficiency Accumulates l-2-Hydroxyglutarate with Progressive Leukoencephalopathy PMC4357467; Struys (2006) JIMD — elevated CSF L-2-HG; L-2-HG inhibits multiple alpha-KG-dependent dioxygenases and the alpha-KGDH complex. | intervention: genetic LoF of L2HGDH: CSF L-2-hydroxyglutarate rises; competitively inhibits mitochondrial alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase -> alpha-KGDH activity decreases
causal:influence:csf_l_2_hydroxyglutarat.mechanism: L-2-hydroxyglutarate (L-2-HG) is a competitive inhibitor of alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent enzymes including the mitochondrial alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (alpha-KGDH). L2HGDH LoF causes L-2-HG to accumulate in CSF, plasma, and urine; accumulated L-2-HG inhibits alpha-KGDH, impairing the TCA cycle at the 2-oxoglutarate step, reducing mitochondrial energy production and driving neurodegeneration.

causal:influence:dhapat_activity:positiv.evidence: Rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata type 2 / RCDP2 (OMIM 222765): biallelic GNPAT mutations abolish DHAPAT activity, causing severely reduced plasmalogen levels in plasma and deficient plasmalogen synthesis in cultured skin fibroblasts (OMIM 222765; PMC10264737 neonatal RCDP type 2). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry ch. 21 (ether-lipid/plasmalogen biosynthesis in peroxisomes). | intervention: do(GNPAT LoF) -> DHAPAT activity falls -> plasmalogen synthesis blocked -> plasma plasmalogen reduced
causal:influence:dhapat_activity:positiv.mechanism: DHAPAT (glyceronephosphate O-acyltransferase, GNPAT) catalyzes the first committed step of plasmalogen biosynthesis in peroxisomes: acylation of dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP). GNPAT deficiency blocks plasmalogen synthesis, reducing plasma plasmalogen levels. More DHAPAT activity drives more plasmalogen production.

causal:influence:dhcr7_activity:negative.evidence: SLOS (Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome) OMIM 270400 (DHCR7 LoF); C-triol is the canonical plasma biomarker of DHCR7 deficiency; Kelley & Hennekam, J Med Genet 2000; Tint et al., 1994 NEJM (7-DHC elevation in SLOS); Irons et al., Lancet 1993. | intervention: DHCR7 loss-of-function (Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome): DHCR7 LoF -> 7-DHC accumulation -> non-enzymatic auto-oxidation to plasma cholestane-3b,5a,6b-triol elevation
causal:influence:dhcr7_activity:negative.mechanism: DHCR7 (7-dehydrocholesterol reductase) reduces 7-dehydrocholesterol (7-DHC) to cholesterol; when DHCR7 is deficient, 7-DHC accumulates and auto-oxidizes non-enzymatically to cholestane-3beta,5alpha,6beta-triol (C-triol). More DHCR7 activity keeps 7-DHC low and thereby reduces C-triol formation.

causal:influence:dihydropyrimidinase_act.evidence: Dihydropyrimidinase deficiency OMIM 222748; van Kuilenburg et al., Biochim Biophys Acta 2004 (dihydrouracil and dihydrothymine elevated in plasma, urine, and CSF in DPYS deficiency patients). | intervention: do(DPYS LoF, OMIM 222748) — dihydrouracil accumulates in CSF
causal:influence:dihydropyrimidinase_act.mechanism: DPYS deficiency causes systemic accumulation of dihydrouracil that crosses the blood-brain barrier; dihydrouracil accumulates in CSF as well as urine and plasma in DPYS deficiency.

causal:influence:dihydropyrimidine_dehyd.evidence: Lehninger, Nucleotide metabolism; van Kuilenburg, Biochim Biophys Acta 2006 (DPD)
causal:influence:dihydropyrimidine_dehyd.mechanism: 5,6-dihydrouracil is the DPYD product from uracil.

causal:influence:gastric_acid_secretion:.evidence: Schubert 2020, Comprehensive Physiology 10(1):197-228, doi:10.1002/cphy.c180035 (low antral pH -> D-cell somatostatin -| gastrin); StatPearls 'Physiology, Gastrin' NBK534822 (pH<3 negative feedback on gastrin) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-134 (23.5: The Stomach): 'Whenever pH levels drop too low, cells in the stomach react by suspending HCl secretion' — acid negative feedback on gastrin loop; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-34.4 (34.4: Digestive System Regulation): 'when the stomach is emptied, the acidic environment need not be maintained and a hormone called somatostatin stops the release of hydrochloric acid. causal:influence:helper_t_cell_activatio.evidence: Mosmann TR & Coffman RL 1989 Ann Rev Immunol 7:145-173 — CD4+ helper T cells provide obligatory activating signals for cytotoxic T cell responses; Reith W et al 2005 J Exp Med 202:1183 — MHC class II deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome): absent helper T cell activation collapses T cell-mediated immunity (OMIM 209920); OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §21.3: 'helper T cells serve as the master regulators of the adaptive immune response' — activation of helper T cells is the gating event for T cell immune activity. | intervention: do(helper_t_cell_activation -) — MHC class II deficiency / CIITA mutation abolishes helper T cell activation and T cell immune activity; do(helper_t_cell_activation +) — checkpoint inhibitor (anti-PD-1) releases helper T cell inhibition, amplifying T cell immune activity.

In MHC class II deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome type II) absent helper T cell activation causes severe combined immunodeficiency with collapsed T cell immune activity.

causal:influence:hematocrit:positive:blo.mechanism: rising packed-cell fraction steeply increases whole-blood viscosity (non-linear)

causal:influence:hepatic_copper_excretio.evidence: OMIM #277900 Wilson disease (raised free/non-ceruloplasmin serum copper); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (Wilson disease: low total but high free serum copper, hepatic copper accumulation); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (hepatobiliary copper excretion)

causal:influence:iduronate_sulfatase_act.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Mucopolysaccharidoses' (MPS II Hunter syndrome: IDS deficiency, elevated plasma/urinary heparan sulfate and dermatan sulfate). causal:influence:il6:negative:plasma_igf.evidence: "IL6 may also cause a decrease in serum IGF1 levels by increasing its clearance through a decrease in IGFBP3 levels" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 25, p. 979

Ch.16 (The Microcirculation and the Lymphatic System: Capillary Fluid Exchange, Interstitial Fluid, and Lymph Flow) §Four Primary Hydrostatic and Colloid Osmotic Forces: “The interstitial fluid colloid osmotic pressure (Pif), which tends to cause osmosis of fluid outward through the capillary membrane.”

causal:influence:intestinal_lactase_acti.evidence: Lancet (PMID:6691) ‘Intestinal pH and propulsion’: lactase deficiency → fecal pH <5.5. Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, Carbohydrate Malabsorption: stool pH <5.5 diagnostic for carbohydrate malabsorption. Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (colonic fermentation of undigested carbohydrates). | intervention: Lactase (LCT) loss-of-function (primary hypolactasia, OMIM 223100) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:intestinal_lactase_acti.mechanism: Lactase (LCT) hydrolyses dietary lactose in the small intestinal brush border. Lactase deficiency (or any intestinal disaccharidase insufficiency) causes unabsorbed carbohydrate to reach the colon, where bacterial fermentation produces short-chain organic acids (lactate, acetate, succinate), lowering fecal pH (<5.5). More lactase activity → more lactose absorbed → less colonic fermentation → higher (less acidic) fecal pH.

causal:influence:leptin:positive:resting.mechanism: leptin activates neuroendocrine and autonomic systems that increase energy expenditure; its absence suppresses expenditure

causal:influence:lipoprotein_lipase_acti.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology, Lipoprotein transport; OMIM 238600
causal:influence:lipoprotein_lipase_acti.mechanism: LPL hydrolysis of TG-rich lipoprotein core lowers plasma triglyceride; LPL or apoC-II loss raises plasma TG (type I/V hyperlipoproteinemia).

causal:influence:mannosyl_oligosaccharid.mechanism: RHEA:55988 (EC 3.2.1.106): N(4)-(Glc3Man9GlcNAc2)-L-asparaginyl-[protein] + H2O = N(4)-(Glc2Man9GlcNAc2)-L-asparaginyl-[protein] + beta-D-glucose; the Glc3Man9GlcNAc2-protein substrate (CHEBI:132537) accumulates as free glucosylated high-mannose oligosaccharides excreted in urine

causal:influence:mast_cell_degranulation.mechanism: Mast cell tryptase (beta-tryptase, TPSB2) is stored in mast cell secretory granules and released into circulation during mast cell degranulation. Plasma/serum total tryptase rises in proportion to mast cell activation (anaphylaxis, systemic mastocytosis). Tryptase is the dominant secretory protein of mast cell granules.

causal:influence:mc4r_activity:negative:.mechanism: MC4R signalling in paraventricular nucleus neurons suppresses food intake via projections to lateral parabrachial nucleus

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: MCAD deficiency (ACADM, OMIM 201450); GeneReviews NBK1424: adipic acid (C6-DC) is the shortest of the three major dicarboxylic acids (adipic, suberic, sebacic) elevated in MCAD deficiency; Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases | intervention: genetic LoF of ACADM gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive MCAD deficiency)
causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.mechanism: MCAD deficiency causes C6 (hexanoate) to be omega-oxidised to adipic acid (hexanedioic acid, C6-DC); reduced MCAD activity raises urinary adipic acid

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: MCAD deficiency (ACADM, OMIM 201450); GeneReviews NBK1424: suberylglycine and hexanoylglycine are the characteristic glycine conjugates of MCAD deficiency; Gregersen et al., Clin. Chim. Acta 1976 (PMID from ScienceDirect): suberylglycine excretion in dicarboxylic aciduria | intervention: genetic LoF of ACADM gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive MCAD deficiency)

causal:influence:monoamine_oxidase_activ.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (serotonin catabolism: 5-HT → 5-HIAA via MAO-A); clinical pharmacology of moclobemide (reversible MAO-A inhibitor): raises synaptic serotonin → antidepressant and anxiolytic effects; OMIM 300615 (MAOB deletion, Norrie disease) and MAOA knockout animal models demonstrate MAO LoF → elevated tissue monoamine levels. | intervention: Pharmacological: moclobemide or phenelzine (MAO-A inhibitors) raise synaptic [serotonin]; MAO-A LoF (e.g., Brunner syndrome mutation p.Arg306Stop, OMIM 300615) → grossly elevated urinary serotonin metabolites confirming direction.
causal:influence:monoamine_oxidase_activ.mechanism: MAO-A (predominant form for serotonin) oxidatively deaminates serotonin (5-HT) to 5-hydroxyindoleacetaldehyde → 5-HIAA; greater MAO-A activity degrades synaptic serotonin, reducing its concentration. causal:influence:monoamine_oxidase_activ.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (dopamine catabolism by MAO to DOPAC and then to HVA via COMT); Knoll J & Magyar K, Adv Biochem Psychopharmacol 1972 (MAO inhibition by selegiline/(-)-deprenyl reduces DOPAC); Levitt P & Bhagavan HN, Psychopharmacol 1975 (MAO inhibitors reduce plasma DOPAC: pharmacological intervention evidence) | intervention: MAO inhibitor treatment (e.g., selegiline/phenelzine): do(monoamine_oxidase_activity=low) -> plasma_dopac falls
causal:influence:monoamine_oxidase_activ.mechanism: monoamine oxidase (MAO, primarily MAO-B in brain and periphery) oxidatively deaminates dopamine to 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, which is further oxidised by aldehyde dehydrogenase to 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetic acid (DOPAC); higher MAO activity raises DOPAC formation; MAO inhibitors (phenelzine, selegiline/deprenyl) pharmacologically reduce plasma DOPAC

causal:influence:muscle_lactate_dehydrog.evidence: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf), Biochemistry, Lactate Dehydrogenase; (Biochemistry, Lactate Dehydrogenase, NBK557536, Function); “The function of the enzyme is to catalyze the reversible conversion of lactate to pyruvate with the reduction of NAD+ to NADH and vice versa.” | LDH interconverts pyruvate and lactate; in glycolytic muscle the LDHA-driven direction makes lactate, so do(LDHA activity up) -> intracellular lactate up (+).

causal:influence:myocardial_contractilit.evidence: Depressed contractility raises atrial/filling pressures (congestive backward failure). causal:influence:ornithine_aminotransfer.mechanism: Ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) catabolizes ornithine to pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C) in the mitochondria; OAT deficiency (gyrate atrophy) blocks ornithine catabolism, causing ornithine to accumulate in plasma, urine, and CSF.

causal:influence:p5c_dehydrogenase_activ.evidence: Farrant RD et al. J Biol Chem 2001 276:15108-15116 (PMID 11134058) — 'Pyridoxal phosphate de-activation by pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid: increased risk of vitamin B6 deficiency and seizures in hyperprolinemia type II'; mechanism confirmed as Knoevenagel condensation of P5C with PLP. PMC9492674 (Comm Biol 2022, Brolese et al.) — new biomarkers for hyperprolinemia type II confirm P5C accumulation and PLP trapping. Frontiers Psychiatry PMC6423912 — 'Intellectual disability associated with pyridoxine-responsive epilepsies': P5C-mediated PLP inactivation reduces AADC and other PLP-dependent enzyme activities. | intervention: do(ALDH4A1 biallelic LoF) = hyperprolinemia type II (OMIM 239500): P5C accumulates → PLP trapped → AADC activity reduced | intervention: do(ALDH4A1 biallelic LoF) — hyperprolinemia type II, OMIM 239500 [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:p5c_dehydrogenase_activ.mechanism: Delta-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate dehydrogenase (ALDH4A1) oxidises pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C) to glutamate. ALDH4A1 LoF (hyperprolinemia type II) causes P5C to accumulate. P5C spontaneously condenses with pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) in a Knoevenagel-type reaction, forming a stable aldamine adduct that inactivates PLP. Since aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC/DDC) requires PLP as an essential cofactor, secondary functional B6 deficiency reduces AADC activity. Sign: more ALDH4A1 activity → less P5C → less PLP trapping → more AADC activity (do(ALDH4A1 LoF) = AADC activity falls).

causal:influence:parasympathetic_tone:ne.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.10 (Rhythmical Excitation of the Heart) §Mechanism of the Vagal Effects: “it decreases the excitability of the A-V junctional fibers ... thereby slowing transmission of the cardiac impulse into the ventricles”
causal:influence:parasympathetic_tone:ne.mechanism: vagal acetylcholine hyperpolarizes A-V junctional fibers, lowering safety factor, delaying or blocking impulse transmission to the ventricles

[citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:phospholamban_level:neg.mechanism: dephosphorylated phospholamban associates with SERCA2a (inhibitory binding disposition) -> lowers SERCA2a apparent Ca2+ affinity (inhibition process) -> reduced SR Ca2+ uptake rate; PLN ablation/overexpression are clean genetic do()

causal:influence:pituitary_acth_secretio.evidence: HumMod endocrine / Boron & Boulpaep HPA axis model plasma ACTH as the corticotroph secretory output into the circulation. Curated by Paul N. Schofield. *** DRAFT FOR REVIEW ***
causal:influence:pituitary_acth_secretio.mechanism: anterior-pituitary corticotroph ACTH secretory output sets the circulating ACTH concentration (mass balance: plasma [ACTH] = secretion − clearance)

causal:influence:plasma_albumin:positive.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (albumin binding of unconjugated bilirubin); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (albumin transport of bilirubin); clinical correlate: low albumin / displacers raise free bilirubin (kernicterus risk)
causal:influence:plasma_albumin:positive.mechanism: unconjugated bilirubin is water-insoluble and circulates tightly bound to albumin; higher plasma albumin increases the bound-bilirubin carrying capacity, raising measured total plasma unconjugated bilirubin (and conversely lowering free bilirubin)

causal:influence:plasma_alpha_ketoglutar.evidence: Alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex deficiency / OGDH deficiency (OMIM 203740): elevated urine alpha-ketoglutarate is a hallmark (MedLink Neurology, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase deficiency review); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 16 (TCA cycle: alpha-ketoglutarate = 2-oxoglutarate, a keto acid; renal organic acid excretion) | intervention: do(OGDH/alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase deficiency)
causal:influence:plasma_alpha_ketoglutar.mechanism: Alpha-ketoglutarate (2-oxoglutarate) is a 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid (keto acid); elevated plasma alpha-KG exceeds the renal reabsorption threshold, spilling into urine and raising total urinary keto acid levels — do(plasma alpha-KG UP) => urinary keto acids UP

causal:influence:plasma_apolipoprotein_c.evidence: Harrison's, Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism (apoC-III as LPL inhibitor / ANGPTL pathway)
causal:influence:plasma_apolipoprotein_c.mechanism: Apolipoprotein C-III inhibits lipoprotein lipase and hepatic remnant uptake; apoC-III excess raises triglyceride-rich lipoproteins.

causal:influence:plasma_biotin:positive:.evidence: Wolf B GeneReviews NBK1322 (biotinidase deficiency, OMIM 253260); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (biotin-dependent carboxylases: PC, ACC, PCC, MCC); StatPearls NBK560607 (biotinidase deficiency — secondary multiple carboxylase deficiency, lactic acidosis); Sweetman L & Williams JC in Scriver's Metabolic Basis of Inherited Disease (multiple carboxylase deficiency). | intervention: do(biotinidase LoF causing secondary biotin deficiency, OMIM 253260)
causal:influence:plasma_biotin:positive:.mechanism: Biotin is covalently attached by holocarboxylase synthetase (HLCS) to the epsilon-amino group of a lysine residue in pyruvate carboxylase (PC), acetyl-CoA carboxylase, propionyl-CoA carboxylase, and 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase. Without biotin, PC cannot bind its CO2 carrier and is catalytically inactive. Biotinidase deficiency (OMIM 253260) prevents recycling of biotin from biocytin, causing secondary biotin depletion and hence multiple carboxylase deficiency — PC LoF leads to impaired gluconeogenesis and pyruvate clearance, producing lactic acidosis and hyperammonaemia. do(biotinidase LoF → plasma biotin ↓) → pyruvate carboxylase activity ↓.

causal:influence:plasma_calcium:negative.evidence: "Even the slightest decrease in calcium ion concentration ... causes the parathyroid glands to increase their rate of secretion within minutes; if the decreased calcium concentration persists, the glands will hypertrophy, sometimes fivefold or more ... Conversely, conditions that increase the calcium ion [concentration reduce gland size]." Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 79 (chw36), p. 988.
causal:influence:plasma_calcium:negative.mechanism: sustained low extracellular Ca2+ drives parathyroid chief-cell hypertrophy/proliferation (glands enlarge fivefold or more in rickets, pregnancy, lactation); conditions that raise Ca2+ decrease gland size -> inverse (negative) control

causal:influence:plasma_calcium:positive.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal handling of calcium; filtered load); Rose & Post, Clinical Physiology of Acid-Base and Electrolyte Disorders (hypercalcemia -> hypercalciuria)
causal:influence:plasma_calcium:positive.mechanism: urinary calcium excretion = filtered load (plasma [Ca] x GFR) minus tubular reabsorption; raising plasma calcium raises the filtered load and thus calcium excretion (e.g. hypercalcemia -> hypercalciuria)

causal:influence:plasma_glucose:positive.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-34.2 (34.2: Nutrition and Energy Production): 'The pyruvate produced during glycolysis is used to synthesize fatty acids. When there is more glucose in the body than required, the resulting excess pyruvate is converted into molecules that eventually result in the synthesis of fatty acids within the body. These fatty acids are stored in adipose cells.'
causal:influence:plasma_glucose:positive.mechanism: excess plasma glucose enters glycolysis yielding pyruvate, which is used for de novo fatty acid synthesis; these fatty acids are stored in adipose cells, increasing fat mass

causal:influence:plasma_glucose:positive.evidence: Hootman KC et al., 'Erythritol is a pentose-phosphate pathway metabolite and associated with adiposity gain in young adults', PNAS 2017;114(21):E4233-E4240 (PMID 28484010; DOI 10.1073/pnas.1620079114). Verified via PubMed/PNAS. Demonstrates endogenous glucose->erythritol conversion by 13C-glucose stable-isotope tracing (ex vivo blood and in vivo dried-blood-spot), with blood erythritol markedly elevated with adiposity gain / elevated HbA1c. Both endpoints ORGAN_SYSTEM scale (same-scale, within-scale edge). Note: the HPO 'decreased CSF erythritol' direction in transaldolase deficiency is set by the PPP enzyme block, a separate enzyme-determined axis not claimed by this core->sink edge.
causal:influence:plasma_glucose:positive.mechanism: Erythritol is synthesized endogenously from glucose via the pentose-phosphate pathway: glucose-6-phosphate -> PPP -> erythrose-4-phosphate -> erythrose -> (reduction) -> erythritol. Higher plasma glucose raises PPP flux and substrate availability, increasing the circulating erythritol pool; CSF erythritol tracks the systemic pool of this small, freely-diffusing polyol. do(plasma glucose up) -> CSF erythritol up.

causal:influence:plasma_insulin:negative.evidence: "Insulin action on glucagon-producing alpha cells suppresses glucagon secretion...demonstrated by deletion of insulin receptors on alpha cells of mice, which leads to mild glucose intolerance, increased glucagon secretion" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 34, p 1719  ||  "DKA is the result of relative or absolute insulin deficiency causing an increase in glucagon concentrations" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 36, p 1436
causal:influence:plasma_insulin:negative.mechanism: Insulin suppresses glucagon secretion from alpha cells via paracrine signalling; insulin receptor KO on alpha cells causes increased plasma glucagon

causal:influence:plasma_myostatin:negati.evidence: "A deficiency of myostatin is responsible for the 'double-muscled' phenotype of Belgian Blue and Piedmontese cattle, and deletion of its gene in mice and humans leads to massive muscle hypertrophy and hyperplasia." — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 2, p 25
causal:influence:plasma_myostatin:negati.mechanism: myostatin (GDF8) negatively regulates skeletal muscle growth; absence of myostatin leads to muscle hypertrophy and hyperplasia (quality: myostatin concentration → disposition: ActRIIB/ALK4/5 signalling → process: SMAD2/3 inhibition of myogenesis → quality: lean body mass)

causal:influence:plasma_nonceruloplasmin.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (Wilson disease: elevated 24 h urinary copper, marked increase after penicillamine challenge); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal handling of non-protein-bound copper)
causal:influence:plasma_nonceruloplasmin.mechanism: ceruloplasmin-bound copper is not filtered, but the loosely-bound non-ceruloplasmin ("free") copper fraction is filtered at the glomerulus and excreted, so a rise in free serum copper (as in Wilson disease, especially under chelation) raises urinary copper excretion

causal:influence:plasma_osmolality:negat.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-157 (26.4: Electrolyte Balance): 'In a negative feedback loop, increased osmolality of the ECF (which follows aldosterone-stimulated sodium absorption) inhibits the release of the hormone.'
causal:influence:plasma_osmolality:negat.mechanism: elevated ECF osmolality (following aldosterone-driven Na reabsorption) inhibits further aldosterone release as negative feedback

causal:influence:plasma_phenylalanine:po.evidence: SIGNOR-264172: phenylalanine (CHEBI:28044) up-regulates tyrosine (CHEBI:18186) via 'precursor of' mechanism (PAH enzymatic conversion). PMID/citation NBK536726 (NCBI Bookshelf: 'Pharmacological Treatment of Parkinson's Disease'): this is an NCBI Bookshelf ID, not a PubMed PMID — pmid_ok=false. causal:influence:plasma_prostaglandin_e2.evidence: "This constriction is aided by reductions in the levels of local and circulating prostaglandins. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs can be given to inhibit prostaglandin synthesis and promote closure... prostaglandins are actually administered to infants... to keep the ductus open." (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 9)

causal:influence:plasma_secretin:positiv.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-136 (23.7: Accessory Organs in Digestion- The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder): 'bile production increases when fatty chyme enters the duodenum and stimulates the secretion of the gut hormone secretin'
causal:influence:plasma_secretin:positiv.mechanism: secretin (triggered by fatty chyme) stimulates bile production and release from the liver

causal:influence:plasma_serotonin:positi.evidence: substances that cause smooth muscle contraction increase pulmonary vascular resistance. These include serotonin, histamine, norepinephrine, and endothelin
causal:influence:plasma_serotonin:positi.mechanism: serotonin contracts pulmonary vascular smooth muscle, narrowing extra-alveolar vessels

causal:influence:plasma_vasoactive_intes.evidence: Bloom et al. (1973) Lancet (original description of VIP-secreting pancreatic tumor causing watery diarrhoea); Said & Mutt (1970) Science (VIP discovery and secretory effects); VIPoma (Verner-Morrison syndrome; OMIM:601634) — autonomous VIP hypersecretion causes profuse secretory diarrhea >1 L/day (WDHA: watery diarrhoea, hypokalaemia, achlorhydria); StatPearls VIPoma (NBK507698); PMC6743256 Fung & Vanden Berghe (2020) review of VIP physiology in GI tract. | intervention: VIPoma (neuroendocrine tumour with autonomous VIP secretion; OMIM:601634): plasma VIP markedly elevated -> intestinal secretion profoundly increased -> secretory diarrhea, hypovolaemia, hypokalaemia; octreotide (somatostatin analogue) suppresses VIP secretion -> diarrhea and intestinal hypersecretion resolve, confirming causal link.
causal:influence:plasma_vasoactive_intes.mechanism: VIP binds VPAC1/VPAC2 receptors on intestinal epithelial cells and submucosal neurons; receptor activation raises intracellular cAMP via adenylyl cyclase -> PKA-dependent phosphorylation of CFTR and Na/K pumps -> active Cl- and water secretion into the intestinal lumen, plus stimulation of pancreatic bicarbonate and enzyme secretion. VIP also inhibits gastric acid secretion. Elevated plasma VIP directly drives intestinal secretion rate.

causal:influence:plasma_vitamin_k:positi.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-40.2 (Components of the Blood): 'Many of the clotting factors require vitamin K to work, and vitamin K deficiency can lead to problems with blood clotting.'
causal:influence:plasma_vitamin_k:positi.mechanism: Vitamin K is required for hepatic gamma-carboxylation of glutamate residues on clotting factors II (prothrombin), VII, IX, and X; without sufficient vitamin K these zymogens are non-functional (PIVKA-II forms instead), reducing thrombin generation in the coagulation cascade.

causal:influence:prpp_synthetase_activit.evidence: PRPS1 superactivity OMIM 300661 (purine overproduction leading to hyperuricaemia; excess IMP pool dephosphorylated to inosine); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (de novo purine synthesis: PRPP -> IMP -> inosine via 5'-nucleotidase); Becker & Kim, J Lab Clin Med 1987 (PRPS superactivity: overproduction of purine nucleotides). | intervention: do(PRPS1 GoF, OMIM 300661) — PRPP overproduction drives IMP accumulation; IMP dephosphorylated to plasma inosine
causal:influence:prpp_synthetase_activit.mechanism: PRPS1 (PRPP synthetase 1) synthesizes PRPP, the committed substrate for de novo purine biosynthesis; PRPS1 superactivity drives overproduction of the purine nucleotide pool (IMP, AMP, GMP). Excess IMP is dephosphorylated by 5'-nucleotidases to inosine, raising plasma inosine levels alongside the known downstream urate overproduction.

causal:influence:pth:negative:osteocyte_.evidence: "Mechanical loading on bone and PTH therapy stimulates bone formation by downregulating sclerostin." — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 30 (PTH/teriparatide anabolic action; sclerostin)
causal:influence:pth:negative:osteocyte_.mechanism: PTH acts on osteocyte PTH1R (quality: plasma PTH → disposition: PTH1R signalling → process: decreased sclerostin (SOST) secretion → quality: osteocyte sclerostin secretion), disinhibiting Wnt/β-catenin and osteoblast activity (basis of teriparatide anabolism)

causal:influence:purine_nucleoside_phosp.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (Nelson & Cox), purine catabolism; PNP deficiency OMIM 613179; Markert, Semin Hematol 1998 (PNP deficiency biochemistry: inosine/guanosine accumulate). | intervention: do(PNP LoF) via biallelic PNP mutations — substrate inosine accumulates
causal:influence:purine_nucleoside_phosp.mechanism: PNP (purine nucleoside phosphorylase) phosphorolyses inosine to hypoxanthine and ribose-1-phosphate; loss of PNP blocks this step, causing inosine to accumulate in plasma (PNP deficiency: severe hypouricemia with inosine/guanosine accumulation).

causal:influence:purine_synthesis_rate:p.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (purine biosynthesis -> nucleotide turnover -> hypoxanthine/xanthine); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology; StatPearls Lesch-Nyhan NBK556079 (opened: de-novo synthesis and unsalvaged purines feed hypoxanthine/xanthine before catabolism to uric acid)
causal:influence:purine_synthesis_rate:p.mechanism: increased de-novo purine production raises the upstream substrate pool (hypoxanthine/xanthine) entering catabolism, raising their plasma levels at fixed downstream XO activity

causal:influence:right_atrial_pressure:n.evidence: "Stretch of the atria also causes significant reflex dilation of the afferent arterioles in the kidneys ... The decreased afferent arteriolar resistance in the kidneys causes the glomerular capillary pressure to rise" -- Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 18 (Nervous Regulation of the Circulation), p 212
causal:influence:right_atrial_pressure:n.mechanism: atrial stretch (raised right atrial/filling pressure) -> reflex dilation of renal afferent arterioles -> lowered afferent resistance -> raised glomerular capillary pressure and filtration (volume reflex)

[citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:salivary_amylase_activi.mechanism: salivary alpha-amylase hydrolyzes dietary starch (alpha-1,4 bonds) to maltose/glucose oligomers, increasing absorbable glucose and postprandial plasma glucose

causal:influence:scot_activity:negative:.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID — SCOT/OXCT1 deficiency (OMIM 245050): persistent non-fasting ketosis
causal:influence:scot_activity:negative:.mechanism: impaired ketolysis raises circulating ketone bodies including 3-hydroxybutyrate; reduced SCOT activity raises plasma 3-hydroxybutyrate

causal:influence:slc30a2_activity:positi.evidence: OMIM 608118 (zinc deficiency, transient neonatal, TNZD; caused by SLC30A2 LoF mutations in the mother); Chowanadisai et al. 2006 / Itsumura et al. 2013 PMC3669329 (compound heterozygous SLC30A2/ZnT2 mutations result in low milk Zn concentrations; ZnT2 mobilises Zn into secretory vesicles in mammary epithelial cells, which is secreted into breast milk); PMC10030689 (novel SLC30A2 mutations in transient neonatal zinc deficiency: ZnT2 essential for mammary gland Zn secretion); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (transient neonatal zinc deficiency due to low breast milk zinc). | intervention: SLC30A2 loss-of-function in lactating mother (OMIM 608118)
causal:influence:slc30a2_activity:positi.mechanism: ZnT2 (SLC30A2) is expressed in the secretory vesicles of mammary gland epithelial cells and transports Zn from the cytoplasm into secretory vesicles, which fuse with the apical membrane to release Zn into breast milk. ZnT2 LoF reduces Zn secretion into breast milk, causing transient neonatal zinc deficiency in the nursing infant. Intervention: do(SLC30A2 LoF heterozygous or homozygous in lactating mothers) -> breast milk Zn >75% reduced.

causal:influence:squalene_synthase_activ.evidence: Squalene synthase deficiency (FDFT1; OMIM 618156); Coman et al., Am J Hum Genet 2018 ( / PMC6037199): 'patients show low blood total cholesterol and reduced low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)' as part of the clinical characterization; GeneReviews NBK553533 (squalene synthase deficiency: 'low total and LDL-cholesterol'). Intervention: do(FDFT1/squalene synthase loss-of-function, OMIM 618156). | intervention: genetic LoF of FDFT1 (squalene synthase; squalene synthase deficiency, OMIM 618156) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:squalene_synthase_activ.mechanism: Squalene synthase (FDFT1) catalyzes the first committed step of the mevalonate pathway leading to cholesterol biosynthesis, condensing two farnesyl-pyrophosphate molecules to squalene. FDFT1 deficiency (squalene synthase deficiency, OMIM 618156) reduces de novo hepatic cholesterol synthesis, lowering circulating LDL-cholesterol. Do(FDFT1 LoF) -> less squalene -> less cholesterol synthesis -> LDL-cholesterol falls. FDFT1 active -> more squalene -> more cholesterol -> more LDL.

causal:influence:steroid_sulfatase_activ.evidence: X-linked ichthyosis (STS deficiency; OMIM 308100): plasma DHEA-S is markedly elevated due to failure of STS to hydrolyse DHEA-S to DHEA. Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, Ch. 15 (DHEA-S <-> DHEA interconversion by STS and SULT2A1). | intervention: STS loss-of-function (X-linked ichthyosis, OMIM 308100): DHEA-S accumulates because it cannot be hydrolysed to DHEA

causal:influence:sympathetic_tone:negati.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.21 (Muscle Blood Flow and Cardiac Output During Exercise; the Coronary Circulation and Ischemic Heart Disease) §Sympathetic Vasoconstrictor Nerves: “When maximally activated, this can decrease blood flow through resting muscles to as little as one half to one third normal”
causal:influence:sympathetic_tone:negati.mechanism: sympathetic vasoconstrictor fibres secrete norepinephrine onto muscle arterioles (alpha receptors), constricting them and reducing resting muscle blood flow

causal:influence:sympathetic_tone:positi.evidence: Guyton1972_Autonomics MODEL0911270005 (AU -> renin); classic sympathetic renin stimulation | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-151 (25.8: Regulation of Renal Blood Flow): 'If blood pressure falls, the sympathetic nerves will also stimulate the release of renin. Additional renin increases production of the powerful vasoconstrictor angiotensin II.'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-41.5 (41.5: Hormonal Control of Osmoregulatory Functions): epinephrine and norepinephrine 'go one step further and trigger the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system' — catecholamines stimulate juxtaglomerular renin release.
causal:influence:sympathetic_tone:positi.mechanism: beta-adrenergic stimulation of juxtaglomerular renin release

causal:influence:testosterone:negative:g.mechanism: testosterone (via aromatization to estradiol) acts at hypothalamic GnRH neurons (via kisspeptin interneurons bearing ERα/AR) to suppress pulsatile GnRH secretion

causal:influence:testosterone:negative:h.evidence: "A greater erythropoietic response to testosterone is associated with stimulation of erythropoietin and suppression of ferritin and hepcidin (a liver-derived peptide that is the main negative regulator of iron bioavailability), possibly resetting the relationship between erythropoietin and hemoglobin and increasing the availability and use of iron for red blood cell production." — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 19, p 751
causal:influence:testosterone:negative:h.mechanism: testosterone suppresses hepatic hepcidin expression, increasing ferroportin-mediated iron efflux and iron availability for erythropoiesis

causal:influence:testosterone:positive:b.mechanism: androgen treatment raises hemoglobin levels; effect mediated by androgen (independent of IGF1 rise)

causal:influence:testosterone:positive:l.evidence: "Decreases in lean body mass, muscle size, and strength were induced by androgen deficiency" (in a study where healthy young-to-middle-age men were treated with GnRH agonist ± testosterone ± aromatase inhibitor). Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 19, p 1339–1341  ||  "testosterone treatment for 1 year that raised testosterone concentrations to the mid-normal range for young men improved…anemia and hemoglobin, volumetric BMD…slightly improved walking distance" and "In a preliminary double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled 12-month trial in men with hepatic cirrhosis found that testosterone improved lean body and bone mass" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 19, p. 724–725
causal:influence:testosterone:positive:l.mechanism: androgen (AR-mediated) increases muscle protein synthesis and lean mass; experimental androgen deficiency by GnRH agonist decreases lean mass

causal:influence:tnf_alpha:negative:plas.evidence: Kern PA, Di Gregorio GB, Lu T, Rassouli N, Ranganathan G. Verified: plasma adiponectin and adipose ADIPOQ mRNA are inversely related to adipose TNF-alpha expression; TNF-alpha is a principal driver of the low-adiponectin state of obesity/inflammation.

causal:influence:troponin_c_calcium_bind.evidence: Bers DM. Excitation-Contraction Coupling and Cardiac Contractile Force (2001); Shannon et al. 2004 (PMID 15347581); OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §19.3.
causal:influence:troponin_c_calcium_bind.mechanism: calcium-bound cardiac troponin C displaces tropomyosin, increases actomyosin cross-bridge recruitment and ventricular force, and thereby increases cardiac output at a fixed loading condition

causal:influence:uroporphyrinogen_decarb.evidence: Harrison's PIM, The Porphyrias (porphyria cutanea tarda: UROD deficiency, elevated urinary uroporphyrin and heptacarboxylporphyrin).
causal:influence:uroporphyrinogen_decarb.mechanism: UROD decarboxylates uroporphyrinogen III; deficiency (porphyria cutanea tarda) causes uroporphyrin (and 7-/hepta-carboxyl porphyrin) accumulation, excreted in urine.

causal:influence:ventilation_perfusion_r.evidence: "the ventilation-perfusion ratio of the unit is gradually reduced ... the CO2 will rise ... the ventilation-perfusion ratio is increased by decreasing blood flow ... the O2 rises and the CO2 falls" — West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 5
causal:influence:ventilation_perfusion_r.mechanism: alveolar PCO2 of a unit is set by its V/Q ratio; reducing V/Q raises CO2 toward mixed venous, raising V/Q lowers CO2 toward inspired gas

causal:influence:ventilation_perfusion_r.evidence: "Now suppose that the ventilation-perfusion ratio of the unit is gradually reduced by obstructing its ventilation, leaving its blood flow unchanged ...
